newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady at 3.05 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady at 3.05 percent.

text.p: German overnight call rates were steady at 3.05 percent on Thursday, fully recovered from end-of-the-month turbulance in June.
Traders said they expected a small increase in customer demand for funds ahead of the weekend and the start of school holidays in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia.
They did not believe, however, that the extra demand would be strong enough to push overnight rates higher.
Traders added the Bundesbank's decision to drain 2.1 billion marks from the banking system on Wednesday was correct in light of existing liquidity.
Rates spiked higher at the end of last month to more than four percent and banks borrowed heavily from the emergency Lombard lending window in strong month-end demand for funds.
Credit institutions held 42.3 billion marks with the Bundesbank on Wednesday, leaving the average for the month so far at 44.2 billion marks.
Banks borrowed only 100 million marks from the Lombard lending facility.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average stood at 3.07067 percent on Thursday compared with 3.07800 percent Wednesday.
